description: TenneT TSO GmbH (hereinafter referred as TenneT) is the largest Transmission System Operator (TSO) in Germany (based on circuit length, installed capacity and size of operating zone as of 31 Decem-ber 2025). Germany and Europe. With its approximately 5,000 employees the company builds, maintains and operates Germany's largest transmission grid with a length over 14,000 km connect-ing more than a third of the European Union’s total offshore wind capacity. The scope of this prequalification procedure covers the supply of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) used in the areas of protection and substation control technology within extra high-voltage and high-voltage substations. The technical requirements are based on internationally recognized substation communication protocols commonly applied in the automation and operation of electrical power systems. The primary focus of the TQS is on IEC 61850, while other relevant protocols, such as IEC 60870 5 103 and IEC 60870 5 104, are also considered where applicable. This prequalification process aims to identify Economic Operators with proven expertise in the planning, production, implementation and integration of such devices in accordance with applicable technical and regulatory requirements. Candidates receive qualification status for each of their own production sites and each technical lot. The successful completion of the qualification process depends on various factors beyond TenneT’s control. TenneT can only commit to the processing time for the individual gates. description: Metroselskabet and Greater Copenhagen Lightrail I/S (hereafter the Client) is procuring a consultancy contract to support and enable the production of a formal method specification for the CBTC systems used on the metro in Copenhagen. The Client intends the use the formal method specification for the following two projects: 1) The future M5 line (requirement specification phase starts in 2024) 2) Resignalling of M1/M2 (3XR) (requirement specification phase starts in 2026-2027). The consultant will be expected to collaborate with other consultants employed by the Client and with the Client´s staff for indentification of generic and specific requirements for the CBTC system, provide training in application of formal methods and will be expected to support and enable the creation and verification of the CBTC formal specification in close cooperation with the Client´s staff. The project is divided into the following Stages: 1) Developing requirement specification for the formal method and testing of the method 2) Implementing the formal method and training of staff (Stage 2). The Client reserves the right to terminate the contract by the end of Stage 1 if the development and testing of the formal method in Stage 1 is not successfully or if it is assessed that the method does not provide the savings expected by the Client. Despite having introduced two driverless metro systems in Copenhagen, the Client has very limited and practical experience with the use of formal methods and formal specifications. The consultant should provide expertise and practical experience within the domain enabling work as "one team" with the Client. This work will be based on the organisation´s experience and knowledge about the functionality and operation. It is the ambition to create the formal specification in close collaboration between the Client and the consultant. The consultant should also provide the necessary training and knowledge of the transfer in process. The Client expects the establishing of formal requirement specifications for the CBTC system will reduce the risk in procurement of such systems as well as reducing the cost to develop and approve the systems, by enabling automation of code generation and efficient safety verification. A formal approach will also help drive the cost down with efficient management of change requests.

title: Germany – Electrical apparatus for switching or protecting electrical circuits – TenneT Qualification System for Protection and Control Systems
description: TenneT TSO GmbH (hereinafter referred as TenneT) is the largest Transmission System Operator (TSO) in Germany (based on circuit length, installed capacity and size of operating zone as of 31 Decem-ber 2025). The company operates critical infrastructure that secures access to a reliable, sustainable and affordable electricity supply. TenneT is one of the largest investors in electricity grids on land and at sea in Germany. Located at the Northwest European energy crossroads, TenneT connects: North and South. Offshore and Onshore. Germany and Europe. With its approximately 5,000 employees the company builds, maintains and operates Germany's largest transmission grid with a length over 14,000 km connect-ing more than a third of the European Union’s total offshore wind capacity. Its growth is driven by a rapidly evolving electricity demand that requires a flexible and growing grid architecture. The scope of this prequalification procedure covers the supply of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) used in the areas of protection and substation control technology within extra high-voltage and high-voltage substations. These devices constitute key components of the secondary technology and are essential for ensuring the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the transmission grid. The technical requirements are based on internationally recognized substation communication protocols commonly applied in the automation and operation of electrical power systems. The primary focus of the TQS is on IEC 61850, while other relevant protocols, such as IEC 60870 5 103 and IEC 60870 5 104, are also considered where applicable. This prequalification process aims to identify Economic Operators with proven expertise in the planning, production, implementation and integration of such devices in accordance with applicable technical and regulatory requirements. Candidates receive qualification status for each of their own production sites and each technical lot. The successful completion of the qualification process depends on various factors beyond TenneT’s control. TenneT can only commit to the processing time for the individual gates. The time required to complete the questionnaires and provide the necessary documentation is the sole responsibility of the participating Economic Operators.

title: Belgium – Passenger cars – Erkenningssysteem voor de aankoop van wagens
description: Om de behoefte aan wagens in te vullen, wil North Sea Port de volgende jaren verschillende voertuigen aankopen met een onderhoudscontract. Het gaat daarbij om 2 types wagens: Poolwagens en Dienstwagens. Er worden wagens ingezet vanuit België en vanuit Nederland. Alle wagens worden aangekocht met onderhoudscontract. Momenteel zijn er een 35tal wagens waarvan ongeveer 20% moeten worden vervangen in 2024. In de daaropvolgende jaren zal er vervangen worden naar behoefte. Ook uitbreiding van dit wagenpark is mogelijk in de nabije toekomst. Hiertoe wordt een erkenningssysteem opgezet: op elk moment kan een geïnteresseerde onderneming een aanvraag tot erkenning indienen waarin zij aantoont dat zij aan de vereisten voldoet. Uiterlijk 30 dagen na de indiening wordt de aanvrager op de hoogte gebracht van zijn erkenning of niet-erkenning. Deze periode wordt geschorst tijdens vakantieperiodes. De voorwaarden voor erkenning kunnen herzien worden, bijvoorbeeld omwille van verandering van technisch omstandigheden (bv. innovaties). Hiervan wordt elke erkende onderneming op de hoogte gebracht zodat tijdig een aanvulling op de aanvraag of een nieuwe aanvraag kan worden ingediend. Omwille van veranderde omstandigheden kan het erkenningssysteem ook worden stopgezet door aanbesteder.
